note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
The Colossians learned the truth “of Epaphras our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ.” That is how they woke up: one brother heard it and said, I am going to teach all of you. Acts 18 shows the same concept at Corinth: “After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth.”

“And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house.” If you were in the synagogue, you were practicing the law of sacrifice. Crispus was the chief ruler of it, and he believed on Christ, just like a lot of us were practicing Christianity and then believed. “And many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.” It started with him and then the others took hold of it.

Paul was actually at Corinth, though. With Epaphras it was different: he was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He said, that is true, I believe it, I am going to go teach it. That is just like today when somebody sees IUIC on YouTube, prints out flyers and starts hitting the city, and then this school pops up and that school pops up. We are the continuation of the acts of the apostles, and when we read these scriptures we have to put ourselves in them, because we are doing the exact same thing.

precepts.point: Think of the faith the Bishop had to have for the truth to be where it is. The impact reaches beyond the purple and gold: outsiders email to donate to the booster club, and every camp watches IUIC at 6 on Saturday night whatever time they teach themselves.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
“And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.” Paul went country to country strengthening all the disciples. That is the job of a leader, and it shows how a leader transfers his belief onto others.

The same work goes on today. As the bishops and the deacons trailblazed the way, the captains follow the same path, and when they go to these places they continue to build our people up worldwide. A captain just back from Guyana reports that the brothers and sisters there in South America are growing tremendously, doing real good. The Lord has good things for them.

Like Paul in Galatia and Phrygia, the leaders go out to the nations where our people are and strengthen the disciples there.

precepts.text: Paul calls Priscilla and Aquila his helpers, who laid down their own necks for his life.
precepts.point: Aquila and Priscilla left Rome, met Paul in Corinth, travelled with him and taught Apollos the way of God more perfectly.

note.label: Civil War & the Son of Perdition

precepts.why:
When Paul came to Corinth he “found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:)”. Rome commanded all the Israelites to leave. That is mass deportation, the same thing Claudius Caesar did back then that you see happening today with Trump and the ICE raids, and they are not raiding Europeans; they are going after the black and Hispanic communities.

But look what Aquila and Priscilla did after they were deported. They sailed with Paul into Syria, evangelizing and doing the work. When they heard Apollos, who only knew John, they “took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.” And Paul writes, “Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus: Who have for my life laid down their own necks”. That brother and his wife were not regular to Paul: they put their own heads on the chopping block for him.

The deportation was a divine mission. The Lord set them up to meet Paul, to teach Apollos, and to help spread the gospel. So don't be scared of no damn ICE. A man's going is of the Lord, and if they take your green card or your citizenship and send you back, it is of the Lord. Brother Nehemiah was deported from France for refusing to stop teaching, labelled an extremist, and now he is doing good in Ghana.

“But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.” Nothing can happen to you unless the Lord allows it. “And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.” Even the bad things happen for good, as the deportation did for Aquila and Priscilla. God has a purpose for every last one of us.

precepts.text: Aquila a Jew born in Pontus, lately come from Italy because Claudius commanded all Jews to depart from Rome; Israelites were strangers in Rome.
precepts.point: People claim Paul wrote to the Romans meaning caucasians, but the scholars say Esau is the forefather of the Roman empire, and the Most High says Jacob have I loved but Esau have I hated. Paul was not writing to the people the Most High hates; he was writing to the Israelites beloved of the Most High who were dispersed and living in Rome as strangers.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Here is one of the strangers of Rome by name: “a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:)”. A Jew born in Pontus, one of the lands on the Pentecost map, who had been living in Italy until Claudius put all the Jews out of Rome.

Israelites were strangers in Rome. They lived there, worked there as tentmakers, and could be commanded to leave, because it was not originally their land; they had been dispersed there. That is what the strangers of Rome means.

precepts.text: A certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, had lately come from Italy, so it was common for Israelites to live in Italy and Rome.
precepts.point: Because the Israelites were scattered through every province and took the names of their captivities, scholars cannot tell a Roman Jewish soldier from a Roman by his name alone, and the New Testament was written in Greek because Israel spoke Greek under the Greeks. Correcting a misheard reference to Luke 3, the centurions of scripture were often Israelite servants in the army.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“There was a certain man in Cesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band.” When our people read “Italian band” they automatically picture a Caucasian. But Caesarea Maritima sat on a seacoast in the land of Israel, and Cornelius was an Israelite officer in the Roman army, not a man of another nation.

It was common for Israelites to live in Italy and Rome. Paul “found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:)”. A Jew born in Pontus, living in Italy, and there were enough Jews in Rome for Claudius to command them all to depart.

Jews of the diaspora were fully enmeshed in Roman culture. They took Greek and Latin names and built careers in the Roman military, so a black man, an Israelite, serving under the Italian band is nothing strange. It is the same as so-called black people and Latinos serving in the American military today, from the Buffalo Soldiers to a general like Colin Powell.

precepts.point: A church just means a gathering or assembly of people. Paul visited Galatia in Acts 16:6 when they went through the region of Galatia, and in Acts 18:23 he went back to strengthen the disciples there.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
Paul went back to Galatia a second time. “And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.”

So there were already disciples in Galatia, the churches, the gatherings of Israelites, and Paul returned to strengthen them. Those are the churches of Galatia he addresses with all the brethren who are with him.

points: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace. So why was Paul dealing with the Corinthians so boldly? Why does he say be not afraid? What were the Corinthians threatening to do? So the Lord had to come to Paul and say, listen, you have got to make your face harder than their face, make your forehead stronger than their forehead, because they are going to try to sway you and intimidate you from teaching the gospel of Christ. And hold not thy peace, meaning do not spare. That is why Paul wrote in 2 Corinthians 13, if I come unto you again I am not going to spare. Because the Lord said, do not hold your peace, do not hold back. Because the Lord knew the Corinthians were wicked.

points: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee. Wait a minute. Paul was bold. He said, the Lord has got me. Y'all can talk your junk all you want. God has got me.

For I have much people in this city. The Lord is assuring Paul that a lot of the Corinthians that we just read about, that did not repent, a lot of them would repent. The Lord has given Paul that confirmation ahead of the ministry.

But that's not why the Lord sent you there. The Lord had you go there to do as he commanded you to do.

points: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city. As dangerous as many of the places we go are, the Lord is with us, and no man is going to hurt you to the point where the mission gets hindered. We go to places we've never touched down before: Zanzibar, Madagascar. When I saw these brothers marching through Madagascar, the spirit it placed on me strengthened me. The Lord used them to strengthen us, as we see brothers going into lands we only thought were stories.

points: And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them. The Lord strengthened him, and he didn't hold back: he taught the commandments of God, he taught Christ. This is the point we're going to get to: missions that are not two weeks or four weeks. The bar is raised, because the diaspora is scattered throughout the four corners of the earth, and who's going to raise them up? Bishop put out the video: there are regions we have not visited yet, congregations with no established sanctuary. We need brothers to go there and teach. We are reading and living the Acts of the Apostles.

Picture shown of the school in Tanzania: look at these children lined up; you tell me these are not the children of Israel. You got some camps out here talking about Israelites are only in America. Tanzania and Zanzibar are 99 percent Muslim lands that never heard that Christ was black, never heard that the Israelites are black, never heard that we should keep the commandments of God. And these children came up saying, we got to hear more; where can we go to hear more? They wanted to be strengthened by the word of God.

points: He departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples. The key is strengthening the disciples.

Do you know how happy the brothers and sisters are in these countries when they see us? It's not money they want. You've been watching Bishop teaching, deacon teaching, captain teaching, and these men show up in your country, in your school, sitting at the same table with you. The joy in their faces. What they want from you is to open the scriptures and strengthen them with the Bible: let them know it's going to be okay, let them know they're not in this alone, let them know that when you leave, you're not going to turn your back on them. All these years they thought, they don't even know we're here. When we show up, that gives them the assurance: they know we're here. We sit, we eat with them, we joke with them, we talk to them face to face, we guide them, we answer their questions.

The sisters' circles the mothers held with the sisters overseas: they love that. Those are the sisters they've been looking up to, now sitting there talking with them face to face. Last year a sister said, now I am at peace; I see the men of God, and she started crying nonstop. She said the Most High kept her alive just to see Bishop. Those are things we take for granted.
